scores.notes: The playing-card guard left of the King has a 3D human head and hat atop a card torso duplicating the King of Hearts with corner 'K' indices, Alice is child-sized instead of giant, and the Rabbit's trumpet floats across his forearm.
A prominent standing prophet with staff lectures weary listeners on the right, inserting the speaker inside his own prophetic words.
An extra fifth speckled sea-turtle flipper protrudes horizontally behind the Mock Turtle's right hind leg.
Paul (with scroll quiver at his waist) sits lecturing five listeners while holding up a mirror as a teaching prop, inserting the epistle's speaker and an audience into the verse's imagery.
A prominent standing prophet with staff gestures rhetorically on the right, inserting the speaker inside his own prophetic words.
A prominent standing prophet with staff gestures toward the rising old man on the left, inserting the speaker inside his own prophetic words.
The priest casts feathers onto the ash pile beside the altar while holding an unbloodied pigeon to honor the brief's no-gore depiction rule; staging and anatomy are clean.
Zoom crop confirms faint horizontal rows of unreadable pseudo-script lines on the left side of the parchment sheet on the table.
In addition to the human face, waistcoat, and bowler hat, the Caterpillar has five asymmetric human arms (two crossed pairs plus a fifth arm sprouting behind its left elbow to hold the hookah).

The round stone slab is shifted back leaving a wide open crescent into the pit while the king presses his signet into a loose mound of mud on top of the slab rather than sealing a closed stone to the rim.

Card soldiers are human men wearing curved cards as sandwich boards, and the far-left 6-of-spades figure has tangled inverted anatomy with black legs and a red cap underneath and headless arms emerging at the top.
Shows Paul with scroll and stylus lecturing eight seated listeners on a terrace with no mirror imagery, inserting both speaker and audience.

Holmes, Watson, and the station-master stride directly away from the burning house behind them while Hatherley points back toward it, and a water jet sprays into a left window out of empty grass with no nozzle or hoseman.
Visible rows of wavy unreadable pseudo-script appear on the desk sheets beside the magnifying glass and on the slip Holmes holds.
Zoom crop confirms unreadable gold glyph-like pseudo-lettering painted across the red side panel of the rightmost fire-engine.
Rows of unreadable wavy pseudo-script appear on Watson's slip, Holmes's letters, and table papers; slight unpainted white paper shows at the bottom-right corner (accepted).
Clear rows of wavy unreadable pseudo-script appear on the top sheet of paper on the foreground desk at bottom left.
Slight unpainted white watercolor paper shows at the bottom-left and top-left corners (accepted).
Slight unpainted white watercolor paper shows at the bottom-right corner (accepted).
Unpainted white watercolor paper vignettes at the left and right edges (accepted).

Both foreground arched card soldiers have upside-down numeral/glyph scribbles ('7', circles, dashes) printed where faces should be, the background-left flamingo has a double-looped neck, and the artwork runs full-bleed to all edges.
All five men march briskly downhill away from the burning house behind their backs while one man gestures backward over his shoulder.

A rooster head merges incoherently onto a playing-card body at bottom left alongside duplicate miniature crowned kings and a garbled dark shape in Alice's hand; zoom crop also confirms wavy unreadable pseudo-script on the floor paper at bottom left.
Watson matches the work's own character sheet rather than a screen actor, while the printed slip he holds up shows a heading bar and neat rows of unreadable tiny pseudo-text.
In the bottom-left foreground, a headless brown bird's wing and tail are fused directly into the back of a playing-card courtier's head.
The blue Caterpillar is drawn with an overtly human old-man face plus a bowler hat and waistcoat not in the text, violating the animal-face depiction rule.
